content: Certain substances have been identified to interfere with the accuracy of continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) systems. For example, acetaminophen, ascorbic acid (vitamin C), and hydroxyurea have been demonstrated to cause inaccuracies in glucose readings on specific CGM devices. Given this potential for inaccuracy, it is essential for individuals using CGM systems to regularly review their medications and supplements with their healthcare provider. Table 7.4 provides a detailed list of substances known to affect CGM accuracy across various device models.
